lessons.title: Styling native controls without losing behavior
lessons.summary: Make the named input inherit the form’s 20px text, use a 200px border box, and preserve label and submit-button behavior.
explanation: Native form controls have browser-provided appearances and do not always inherit page typography in the way ordinary text does. Explicit font: inherit can make their text consistent while preserving their native editing and activation behavior.

font: inherit copies the parent’s computed font settings. border-box makes the declared input width include padding and border. min-height reserves room without pretending that one height fits every language or zoom setting. Keep the label association, name and button type in HTML. Do not remove native appearance or focus indicators merely to make the control look like a painted rectangle; appearance can vary across browsers.

lessons.title: Recognizable link states
lessons.summary: Keep the link underlined before interaction and add a 3px keyboard-focus outline without removing its href.
explanation: Links should remain recognizable without requiring a particular color perception. An underline provides a non-color cue. Hover and keyboard focus are different states; a visible focus outline should not depend on moving a pointer.

The base underline remains when no interaction state applies. :active means the link is being activated, not the page currently being viewed. :visited may style some properties for links in history, but browsers deliberately hide visited-state details from scripts to protect privacy. Do not test someone’s browsing history with computed styles or selectors. This task does not grade visited colors.
